text:
Starling is the best all-round main UK current account, offering complete traditional banking features (joint accounts, overdrafts, Post Office cash/cheque deposits, and full Current Account Switch Service support) with zero monthly fees. Chase is the stronger choice if you want to maximize cashback and savings on everyday spending, while Revolut works best as a secondary travel or multi-currency account rather than a primary UK bank.

International Transfers	Yes (0.4% + small delivery fee)	Not supported	Yes (strongest multi-currency & transfer tools)
Which One Fits Your Setup?

Choose Starling as your main hub if: You want a reliable, no-nonsense primary bank where your salary lands and Direct Debits go out. It is the only one of the three that feels like a complete replacement for a high-street bank—supporting joint accounts, a competitively priced overdraft, cheque imaging, Post Office cash deposits, and 24/7 UK customer support.   
Generation Money

Choose Chase as your main spender if: You don't need a joint account, overdraft, or international wire transfers, and want to earn passive rewards. Its 2% cashback on everyday essentials (provided you meet the monthly deposit/payment requirements) and boosted linked saver make it one of the most lucrative free accounts for daily spending.   
The Finance Lowdown
+ 1

Choose Revolut if: You frequently hold, convert, or transfer multiple currencies, or want stocks, commodities, and crypto trading inside your banking app. While Revolut now holds a full UK banking licence with FSCS protection, its free Standard tier has strict weekend exchange markups and ATM caps, meaning you either have to pay for a monthly plan or treat it as a secondary app.   
Generation Money
+ 1

The Optimal Hybrid Setup: Many UK users use Starling as their core salary and bills account (taking advantage of Spaces for bills and joint account options), and transfer a monthly spending allowance to Chase to capture the 2% cashback and boosted savings interest.
